A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that conscious perception of complex images is the result of two processes, state and strength.

conscious experience is the result of the interaction between two independent processes, one of which reflects the discrete nature of the mental state and the other of which reflects the continuous nature of mental strength.
the state-strength framework provides an integrated account of the processes underlying memory and perception.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the processes that give rise to conscious experience are continuous and can be measured using psychophysical methods.
subjective experience is not a reliable guide to the underlying cognitive processes.
conscious states and cognitive strengths are not only distinct processes, but that each is also necessary to explain the behavior of the other.
